Steven Shwartz (born September 16, 1953) is an American entrepreneur, award-winning author on artificial intelligence, and angel investor.
Early life and education
Shwartz was born on September 16, 1953. He earned a Bachelor of Science in Experimental Psychology from New College of Florida. He then completed a Ph.D. in Cognitive Science at Johns Hopkins University in 1979, conducting research on visual imagery under Professor Stephen Kosslyn. Following his doctorate, Shwartz undertook postdoctoral research in artificial intelligence at Yale University’s Computer Science Department under Roger Schank.
Career
In 1981, Shwartz became the first employee and Vice President of Software Development at Cognitive Systems, founded by Roger Schank to commercialize natural language understanding; the company completed an initial public offering in 1986.
In 1984, he co‑founded Intelligent Business Systems, which developed EasyTalk, a natural language interface to SQL interface recognized as a “breakthrough technology” by Gartner Group in 1987. In 1991, he founded Esperant Technologies which developed menu-driven natural language interface for SQL. The company was acquired by Software AG in 1993.
Shwartz joined Transcentive in 2001, an equity compensation management provider later acquired by Computershare in 2004; he served as Global CTO and General Manager of the Transcentive division for five years. In 2013, he co‑founded Device42, which craeted IT asset management software. He retired from day‑to‑day operations in 2020 but remained Board Chair until Device42 was acquired by Freshworks for $230 million in 2024.
As an early investor and board member at Tangoe, a telecom expense management firm, Shwartz helped the company achieve a successful IPO in 2011 and guided it to over $200 million in revenue.
Volunteer work
Shwartz is involved in volunteer work and serves on several non-profit boards. He is the Board Chair of Marrakech Inc., an organization that offers services to more than 1,000 individuals with intellectual and other disabilities.
